results.controlIntent: [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] are used to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system; and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals multiple violations of CM-3(1).r4's automated change-control requirements:

**Violation 1 — Hotfix deployed without registry approval (critical):**
The `UpdateEndpoint` event (2026-03-15T14:22:00Z, user: data-scientist-jdoe, config: churn-predictor-v1-hotfix) has no corresponding model registry entry. This directly violates sub-controls (b) notify approval authorities, (d) prohibit changes until approvals are received, and (e) document all changes. A change was pushed to production with no evidence of a documented proposal, approval gate, or registry lineage.

**Violation 2 — Initial deployment sequencing concern:**
The `CreateEndpoint` event (2025-12-01T11:00:00Z) carries an embedded audit annotation stating the endpoint was "Deployed 2h BEFORE registry approval at 09:00." While the raw timestamps show 11:00 > 09:00 (deployment after approval), the presence of this audit flag in the CloudTrail record indicates the automated change-control mechanism itself recorded a sequencing anomaly — suggesting the approval gate did not enforce the correct pre-deployment block.

**Overall assessment:** The automated mechanisms required by CM-3(1).r4 — specifically the gate that prohibits deployment until approval is received (sub-control d) and the requirement to document all changes through the registry (sub-control e) — were bypassed for the hotfix update. The control is not satisfied.
gaps: No registry entry exists for the hotfix config 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' — it is unknown whether an out-of-band approval process (e.g., ticket system, change advisory board) was used; human attestation would be needed to rule this out.

The embedded audit note on the CreateEndpoint event is ambiguous — human review of the change-control system logs at the time of initial deployment would clarify whether the approval gate was enforced or bypassed.
No evidence of automated notification to personnel upon completion of approved changes (sub-control f) was available from the collected evidence.
No evidence of a time-bound escalation mechanism for unapproved changes (sub-control c) was available.
